reference_sql:
SELECT channel, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_ts >= DATE '2026-01-05' - INTERVAL 29 DAY
  AND order_ts < DATE '2026-01-05' + INTERVAL 1 DAY
GROUP BY channel
alternatives: SELECT channel, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE CAST(order_ts AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-07' AND DATE '2026-01-05' GROUP BY channel
SELECT channel, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE CAST(order_ts AS DATE) > DATE '2026-01-05' - INTERVAL 30 DAY AND CAST(order_ts AS DATE) <= DATE '2026-01-05' GROUP BY channel

other_way.sql: SELECT channel, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE CAST(order_ts AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-07' AND DATE '2026-01-05' GROUP BY channel
other_way.tradeoff: Typing both end dates reads clearly, but counting back from the as-of date with an INTERVAL shows where the 30 days come from.
